answers.ask: What should the maps look like - military, urban, sci-fi, something else?
answers.answer: Use a military theme for all three maps, matching the gun-game combat.

answers.ask: Should all three maps share a lane layout, or should they differ (open, close-quarters, vertical)?
answers.answer: Have the three maps differ: one open, one close-quarters, and one with vertical areas, so the vote gives players distinct choices.

scene_prompt: Create three distinct military-themed combat maps for players to choose between: one open map with broad sightlines and sparse cover, one close-quarters map built from tightly connected structures and narrow passages, and one map with elevated areas and multiple vertical routes.
agent_notes: Two teams, shared loadouts and most-kills-on-a-timer is Team Deathmatch, and the round-based lobby does not make this Party & Casual — the game is guns and sightlines. I swapped the preset's lane-network for space-staged because the vote happens in a waiting area players then teleport out of, and because the answers say the three maps should differ (open, close-quarters, vertical) rather than share one lane layout, so a single lane shape would be a lie about two of the three. P4 is earned outright here by the teleport and the three distinct arenas, so there is no continuous-map override to apply; cover-elevated covers the vertical map and stays tiered rather than overhanging. Without a user I took the military theme from the answers, treated the 130-second timer, the 30-second minigun and the sniper/grenade loadout as gameplay with no layout geometry, and read the spawns as two shielded team bases per arena.
